input.quote: (iv) Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement or (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Kubient control with respect to Kubient's obligations hereunder.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position; no redline. Section 10(a) (p0047) is a genuine Vendor-side obligation to "indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees" against all third-party Claims, including reasonable attorneys' fees. IP infringement is covered, even though the indemnity does not use the words "intellectual property infringement" in its own list: (i) the limbs at 10(a)(i)-(ii) cover Claims "arising out of or in connection with" the Services and the Auction Platform, which captures a third-party allegation that the Service infringes; and (ii) limb 10(a)(iv) picks up "Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty," which incorporates the express non-infringement warranty at Section 9(b)(i) (p0033) that "the Service and any deliverables provided hereunder by Kubient do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party." The same limb pulls in Vendor-caused data-breach exposure (9(b)(iii), p0035) and Vendor's breach of applicable Law (9(b)(ix), p0041), while limb 10(a)(v) reaches the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors, covering Vendor negligence and misconduct. The indemnity therefore reaches all four elements of the preferred position rather than excluding IP; the failed keyword check reflects drafting style, not a gap in scope. Section 11 (p0053-p0055) supplies the expected procedure: prompt notice that is expressly not a condition to recovery, indemnitor control of defence and settlement, no settlement admitting our liability without our written consent, and cooperation at the indemnitor's cost. No sub-cap or super-cap applies, and Section 7(a) (p0027) expressly carves indemnification liability out of the consequential-damages exclusion, so the fallback 3x-fees super-cap is unnecessary. The Customer-side indemnity at 10(b) (p0052) is an acceptable mirror keyed to our Content and Properties, our unauthorised or inappropriate use, and our own breach. Two minor sub-elements are noted rather than flagged: the "acts or omissions of Customer" limb at 10(b)(v) is marginally wider than the playbook's ideal narrow Customer indemnity, and the Creative limb at 10(a)(iii) is softened by "to the best of its knowledge." Neither is material given the clause as a whole meets the preferred position.
